subject: Recap & mutual action plan — Arbora latency, throughput & topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@arbora.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & mutual action plan — Arbora latency, throughput & topology

Thanks again for the call earlier, Emily. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I pulled notes from the convo with Simon and your infra team. TL;DR: you need predictable p95 latency for live inference (chat + summarization) at scale, while keeping costs under control for non-critical workloads.

Key pain points we captured:
- Tight p95 target for the UI: ~250ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), 450ms for 1–2k token contexts (current system spikes unpredictably).
- Peak concurrency pattern: 800–1,200 concurrent active users in US region during spikes; typical sustained QPS ~120–200.
- Long-tail contexts (docs + chat history) increase memory and KV pressure — this is your main ops pain.
- Compliance: certain customers require data residency and strict audit logs.

Agreed goals:
- Target p50/p95 for user-facing generation: 80ms / 250ms for short prompts; p95 <= 450ms for longer contexts for the MVP.
- PoC scale: demonstrate stable 95th percentile under 1,000 concurrent users with automated fallback.
- Show cost delta and latency tradeoffs between (a) quantized Llama-variant on dedicated pool, (b) higher-accuracy 13B open models in multi-tenant mode.

Technical summary / immediate recommendations (high level):
- Topology: hot-path dedicated GPU pool for latency SLOs + warm multi-tenant pool for heavy batch/rerank workloads.
- KV/prefix caching: cache most recent 3 messages and static doc embeddings; TTL 15–30m to lower KV hot reads.
- Batching & streaming: continuous batching with a short batching window (target 12–20ms) + streaming for UI so p50 stays low.
- Quantization: evaluate int8 first (good balance) and 4-bit where quality permits. We'll quantify quality delta on your eval set.
- Fallbacks: route to cheaper, lower-capacity model variant if queues > threshold or during cross-region failover.

Next steps we proposed on the call (action owners in parentheses):
1) Arbora to share: minimal production prompt set + 200 representative conversation traces and PII questionnaire (Emily) — we referenced the attached "arbora_poc_requirements.xlsx" and "arbora_pii_questionnaire.pdf".
2) Redwood to deliver: PoC sketch (resource sizing + costs) and a topology diagram + test plan (Marissa) by EOD Thu 21 Mar.
3) Technical deep-dive with infra + model ops (Karthik + Sean) — schedule for next week; proposed 60-min slot.
4) Define pass/fail for PoC: 95th percentile under 450ms at 1k concurrent with correct routing and logs available to Arbora’s SOC (shared responsibility).

Attachments: arbora_poc_requirements.xlsx, arbora_pii_questionnaire.pdf.

If this summary looks accurate I’ll drop the PoC sketch and cost estimate into the HubSpot deal and propose 2–3 meeting times for the deep-dive.

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap & mutual action plan — Arbora latency, throughput & topology

Looping in technical notes from my side after reviewing the sample traces and the ask. High-level technical posture we should take for the PoC:

1) Model & quantization
- Start with a 13B Llama-variant (the one Emily referenced) quantized to int8 for the latency-first pool. Run a parallel eval with an 8-bit and a 4-bit build to chart quality drop vs throughput improvement.
- Keep a baseline (non-quantized or int16) for the long-context batch jobs where latency is not primary.

2) Serving topology
- Dedicated hot-path pool: pinned GPUs (2–4 x A100 equivalent for PoC), multi-instance with KV cache collocated on node-local NVMe (fast TTL). This gives predictable p95 behavior.
- Warm multi-tenant pool: auto-scale based on queue depth and scheduled batch windows. Use cheaper instance types for rerank/batch inference.
- Fallback & routing: policy-based routing by request tag (ui-interactive vs background). For UI tags, enforce a queue-depth threshold to trigger fallback model.

3) Batching & streaming settings
- Continuous batching with 12–20ms batch window target; allow micro-batch bypass for single-token streaming when p50 is critical.
- Max batch size capped per GPU to avoid OOMs; measure throughput via PoC harness.

4) KV cache strategy
- Cache compressed KV segments for repeated conversation prefixes with TTL 900–1800s. Use LRU eviction and tag-based invalidation when user edits context.

5) Observability and SLOs
- Telemetry: token-level latency, queue depth, kernel-time vs queue-time split, cache hit ratio. Export to Arbora’s Grafana via a read-only view for the PoC.
- SLO alerting: p95 breaches should trigger automated scale-up and a non-blocking rollback to fallback model if not recovered within 30s.

Action items I propose for the PoC runbook (owners/dates):
- Redwood: initial resource sizing + cost delta (Marissa) — deliver by Thu 21 Mar.
- Redwood: build small load harness to reproduce 1k concurrent profile (Karthik) — sketch by Fri 22 Mar, run week of 25 Mar.
- Arbora: finalize and send sanitized prompts + target eval metrics (Emily) — by Wed 20 Mar.

I attached a quick topology sketch (slo_topology_sketch.png) and will add an initial test harness plan to the HubSpot link. Thoughts?

–Karthik
